question: Can a fresh isolated WSLc session run a pinned Python image with network disabled and a read-only host bind mount, verify bytes, and reject writes?
success_criteria: pinned image metadata resolves after one explicit pull in the named session
one container run exits zero with expected marker and EROFS for write attempt
exact-CID cleanup query confirms no match
failure_criteria: any timeout, session start failure, missing/malformed CID, nonzero run, unexpected write success, cleanup ambiguity, or session termination ambiguity => HOLD/UNKNOWN; no retry
allowed_operations: read local version and resource facts
create/start one named nonpersistent session with wslc system session enter --name and this attempt-owned storage path
inspect exact image within that named session
one pull of the exact pinned image into that session
one bounded run with network none, requested 512M memory and 1 CPU, read-only mount, --rm, exact unique name and cidfile
query exact CID only if receipt exists
remove only this session exact image and terminate only this named session after verified container absence
prohibited_operations: access or cleanup of any other session/container
cleanup: verify exact CID absence then remove exact pinned image in named session; terminate only named session; preserve logs and receipts
nonclaims: does not test Windows GUI input delivery or release
does not test environment reaction or finite recovery
does not establish cgroup or swap enforcement
one smoke sample does not establish reliability

allocation.session_creation: wslc system session enter --name <unique-session> <attempt-owned-storage-path>; keep shell open until commands and cleanup finish; exit only at the end
allocation.initial_session_inspect_result: WSLC_E_SESSION_NOT_FOUND because the new named session had not yet been created; no image pull or container run occurred
